subject: ACME POC: eval methodology & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: eval methodology & next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed next steps plan so we can lock the POC timeline. High-level goals we heard:
- Validate accuracy and hallucination rate for our LLM on your retrieval-enhanced prompts
- Measure latency under representative production traffic
- Estimate per-call cost at target throughput

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Accuracy / correctness >= 92% on ACME grading rubric (weighted)
2) Hallucination rate <= 3% on randomized acceptance set
3) P95 latency <= 450ms for single-request inference in shadow mode
4) Cost-per-1k-tokens estimate within 20% of forecast

Evaluation approach (recommended):
- Offline evaluation (2 weeks): we run the submitted prompt set and ACME-provided annotated examples against candidate models. We provide per-sample grades and aggregate metrics.
- Online shadow (1 week): mirror a sample of live traffic to Redwood in shadow-only mode to capture latency and end-to-end behavior with production payloads (no responses returned to users).

Ownership and roles:
- ACME: Priya Shah (product lead) provides samples and acceptance labels, Jordan coordinates scheduling and legal (NDA).
- Redwood: Marissa (PM) will own the evaluation plan and delivery; Dylan (engineer) will own the infra and shadow setup; Rachel (evals) will help design grading rubric and analysis notebooks.

Attachments: acme-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf (proposed timeline & deliverables), acme-eval-grading-rubric.xlsx (draft weights).

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm rubric and sample set this week (target: Thu 6/18)
- Start offline eval on Mon 6/22 (2 weeks)
- Run online shadow the week of 7/6 (1 week)
- Wrap & review results week of 7/13

Can you confirm the success criteria and the timeline, or suggest adjustments? Also let me know if you need any additional compliance paperwork before shadowing (we can provide SOC2 evidence / DPA pointers).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions PM, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: eval methodology & next steps

Marissa — quick technical notes from my side:

- Online shadow: we can support mirrored traffic with token-level logging + request ids. We'll need a VPN endpoint or allowlist for ACME IPs; typical setup takes 2-3 business days once paperwork is signed.
- Data handling: shadow payloads will be stored in a secured S3 bucket with retention configurable per ACME policy; we can provide KMS-wrapped keys.
- Offline eval: recommend providing a 500-1,000 sample set for the first pass. We can batch-run with deterministic seed and provide per-sample annotations and anonymized logs.

Suggested grading rubric (technical):
- Accuracy / relevance: 50%
- Hallucination / factuality: 20%
- Latency (request-level p95): 15%
- Robustness (edge-case prompts): 10%
- Cost estimate deviation: 5%

Notes on latency target: P95 <= 450ms is achievable for the smaller models; for larger backbones we may need quantization to hit that consistently. We should identify 2 candidate model variants (fast+accurate) before offline eval.

I can spin up the shadow test harness once we lock the start date and legal. Attaching a short infra checklist in the plan PDF.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: eval methodology & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of small asks:

- Can you share the sample grading rubric with explicit acceptance thresholds (e.g., what constitutes 92% accuracy vs. 90%)? The attached XLS looks like weights but not thresholds.
- We need to shift the offline start to Mon 6/22 (that works), but can we run the shadow the week of 6/29 instead of 7/6? Our release window means we can provide a continuous sample earlier.
- I'll share an initial 400-sample set by EOD Fri 6/19. Priya will be the single point to review labels.
- We have an internal security checklist — I'll send that to Dylan; I expect the VPN/allowlist flow will be fine.

Also, legal would like a one-page summary of data retention and deletion after the POC. If you can include that in the plan PDF that would speed approval.

Jordan Ellis

Great — thanks Jordan, that all sounds reasonable. Summary of agreed changes and next steps: 

1) Rubric: Rachel will add explicit acceptance thresholds to the XLS (e.g., pass >= 92% accuracy; marginal 88-92%; fail < 88%) and include example anchor cases. Expect updated rubric by Fri 6/19 EOD.
2) Timeline: Offline eval start Mon 6/22 (2 weeks). Online shadow moved up to week of 6/29 (1 week). Wrap & review week of 7/6.
3) Samples: Jordan to send initial 400 samples by 6/19. We'll confirm any format conversions needed.
4) Infra/legal: Dylan will coordinate the allowlist and provide a one-page data retention/deletion summary for legal.
5) Deliverables: Updated plan PDF, rubric XLS, shadow infra checklist, and a short runbook for reproducing offline eval. Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-42, drive folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePOCSharedDrive

I've attached updated plan and rubric v1 to this thread (acme-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf, acme-eval-grading-rubric.xlsx). If everyone is aligned I'll open a HubSpot task to track the milestones and create the shared results notebook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
